description: Generate audiobooks from EPUBs, PDFs and text with synchronized captions.

summary.one_liner: Abogen is a text-to-speech tool that converts EPUB, PDF, text, markdown, and subtitle files into audio with matching synchronized subtitles, using Kokoro-82M.
summary.what_it_does: Abogen takes ePUB, PDF, .TXT, .MD, .SRT, .ASS or .VTT input (via drag and drop or a built-in text editor) and generates speech using Kokoro-82M. It can output WAV, FLAC, MP3, OPUS, or M4B with chapters, and writes SRT or ASS subtitles with configurable granularity from line-level to word-level. Chapters can be selected and saved as separate files or merged, and M4B metadata and cover art are taken from EPUB and PDF files. It has a PyQt6 desktop GUI (abogen) with queue mode and a voice mixer for blending voices, plus a Flask web UI (abogen-web) with a background job queue, LLM-assisted text normalization, and Audiobookshelf upload. A CLI (abogen-cli) is available for troubleshooting.
use_cases: Turn an EPUB or PDF into an audiobook
Create voiceovers for social media videos
Batch convert multiple documents to audio
Convert SRT or VTT subtitle files to speech
how_to_run: Install espeak-ng (Windows: run the .msi from its latest release; Mac: brew install espeak-ng; Linux: apt/pacman/dnf install espeak-ng)
Windows option 1: download the repo and run WINDOWS_INSTALL.bat
uv tool install --python 3.12 abogen (Linux, or Windows without GPU; add [cuda] extras for NVIDIA on Windows)
Run abogen for the desktop GUI, or abogen-web for the Web UI
Docker: docker build -t abogen . then docker run with port 8808 mapped
notable: Desktop GUI and Flask web UI, each with a different feature set
Synchronized subtitles at word, sentence, comma, or line granularity (word-level English only)
Voice mixer to blend voice models with weights and save profiles
Chapter markers and timestamp-based text files for timed narration
Optional LLM normalization via any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Audiobookshelf integration in the web UI
caveats: Windows AMD GPU acceleration is not supported; AMD needs Linux with ROCm
Word-level subtitle modes are English only, because Kokoro provides timestamps only for English
The desktop app lacks some features (e.g., Supertonic TTS, LLM normalization, Audiobookshelf) that exist only in the Web UI
